subject: general
question: At what annual simple interest rate will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a sum of money to double itself, the simple interest earned must be equal to 100% of the principal.

Shortcut formula: Rate × Time = 100

Rate = 100 ÷ Time

Rate = 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5% per annum.

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 8 years

Amount (A) = 2 × Principal (P)

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 Amount (2P)
 

 Time = 8 Years
 
 SI = 2P − P = P

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = Amount − Principal

⇒ SI = 2P − P = P

⇒ P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 1 = (R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 8

⇒ R = 12.5%

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Formula for 'n' times

To calculate the rate R for a sum to become n times in time T: R = (n − 1) × 100 ÷ T.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount A is given by P + SI, which can be expressed as A = P(1 + RT/100).

Rule of 72 for Compound Interest

A quick way to estimate the time required to double money with CI is T ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.</p
